title: Enterprise VPC latency wave during microburst traffic
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: A large enterprise customer on a VPC private deployment reported repeated 10-30s TTFT spikes and a 3-5x drop in tokens/sec during short traffic microbursts. The pattern was visible across Hosted/Dedicated/private nodes that service pinned model variants. This ticket centralizes the triage, short-term mitigation, and full RCA + follow-ups.

Observed behavior: latency waves last 2-6 minutes, recur several times per hour, aligned with small burst traffic (peak QPS < 200) consisting of many short streaming requests (context length ~1-16). During waves we observe: elevated first-token latency, KV cache miss rates spike, continuous-batching pipeline throughput collapses, and autoscaler incorrectly scales down several GPU workers followed by slow warmup.

Why this is urgent: customer SLOs (first-byte < 250ms) breached repeatedly; customer has dedicated SLA and legal escalation in flight. Engineering must ship a safe hotfix to stop regression for all environments and a permanent fix to the batching/idle-detection heuristics.
reproduction_steps: Replay small-streaming workload with high fanout: 90% streaming requests, median context 4 tokens, bursts of 100-200 RPS lasting ~30s every 5-10 minutes (use loadgen profile attached)
Route traffic through VPC edge-router with per-tenant prioritization enabled (customer's config) to reproduce routing behavior
Observe metrics: first_token_latency, tokens_per_sec, kv_cache_hit_rate, continuous_batch_size, worker_cpu_util, gpu_util, autoscaler_decision_trace
Run with both runtime-2.3 and runtime-2.4 to see behavioral delta (regression introduced between releases)

mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): throttle microburst small-streaming requests into explicit microbatches at edge-router (config flag) to preserve continuous-batching path
Short-term (hotfix): increase autoscaler idle hold to 90s and disable scale-down when average continuous_batch_size < 1.5 across last 3 intervals for pinned pools
Immediate rollback option: pin affected customer traffic to dedicated warm pool (already applied for the escalated customer)
Medium-term: ship runtime patch that restores batching fallback for streaming-without-prefetch and adds KV cache prewarm on worker startup
rollout_plan: Step 1 — Canaries: deploy hotfix flag to 5% of traffic in hosted region, observe first_token_latency and tokens/sec for 1 hour
Step 2 — Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 3 deployments if metrics stable, each step 30 minutes
Step 3 — Dedicated/private: release configuration artifact (edge-router + autoscaler flags) to Dedicated accelerator pools, then to Private via customer-specific package
Step 4 — Customer validation: confirm with escalated customer and 2 other large customers before full global ramp
Rollback — revert flag and return pinned routing if any regression detected during canary
root_cause_analysis: Regression introduced in runtime-2.4: a prioritization change aimed at low-latency streaming inadvertently bypassed the continuous-batching admission path for short-streaming requests while still incrementing idle counters for workers. This caused small requests to form many tiny microqueues that prevented efficient batching, drove KV cache miss rate up (cold entries due to frequent transient worker restarts), and triggered autoscaler idle logic to scale down pooled workers prematurely. The net effect: repeated first-token stalls and reduced tokens/sec during microbursts. The heuristic change passed unit tests but lacked an integration test for mixed streaming + batching workloads.
postmortem_actions: Ship integration test that replays mixed streaming+batching workload and asserts continuous_batch_size and autoscaler stability
Add telemetry alert for 'small-streaming-burst-to-batch_ratio' and 'autoscaler-scale-down-during-burst' with automated paging
Revert greedy prioritization change and implement safer admission gate that respects batching eligibility
Add a rollout checklist: include per-tenant VPC mirror tests and a warmup KV cache verification step
Document the temporary flags and remove them within 30 days after stable rollout
Schedule postmortem review with product & SRE and update runbooks for VPC-dedicated customer escalations
